Ready for the maintainer to merge. Safety-tier review. No blocking findings.

I read the complete diff and checked the current upstream laws. The acknowledgment checks the source and stock fingerprints. The exception applies only when the program stays in one setup on the column engine. Changed columns remain gouges. Opening a project clears the acknowledgment.

Checks ran locally in `.claude/worktrees/review-4066`. Trial merge: `dd94e64824b08c6ec20e65932f5579bf2fa13968`, with upstream main `aef12fea67e0082e7ba835a3d9fcade8e2c11eb0`. Its first parent is the reviewed PR head.

- Quick gate: 354 steps; 2,828 tests passed, 36 ignored, one pre-existing failure. All 350 app suites passed.
- App unit tests: 315 passed. These include the fresh-gouge and lattice checks.
- `keep_law`: 36 passed, including all five new acknowledgment tests.
- UI `operations`: 31 passed. UI `shell`: 20 passed, one failed.
- App clippy, all targets, with `-D warnings`: passed.
- Release light lane: all six steps passed; 11 tests passed. Steps: motion `lib`, `adaptive_troch_island`, `adaptive_troch_neck`, `adaptive_troch_parallel`, and app `pocket_pass_start`, plus the build.

Extra suites run:

- `example_catalog`: 43 passed, four ignored.
- `example_catalog_edge_work`: one passed.
- `solid_law_goldens`: seven passed.

These suites ran by name in the quick gate. No fixture or importer change requires additional kernel suites. No golden or recorded program changed in this PR. Full heavy lanes were not run, as the current law reserves them for the cut.

Safety input mutations, run locally through the PR tests:

- Remove the acknowledgment: posting is RED as expected; the control test is GREEN.
- Add the bore that deepens the incoming step by 3 mm: posting is RED as expected; the located-gouge test is GREEN.
- Keep the acknowledged step unchanged: posting is GREEN with the located 5.00 mm note.
- Reopen the project: posting is RED again; the reset test is GREEN.

No source-code mutation was applied.

Pre-existing failure:

`crates/ui/tests/shell.rs:12`, `headless_cli_exit_code_is_zero`, fails with:

```text
assertion `left == right` failed
  left: 1
 right: 0
```

I ran the same complete shell suite on bare upstream main `034e91b8b78fa64989d18e1d5d17344531c4762c`. It has the same failure, with 20 tests passed and one failed. This host failure does not block this PR. I did not identify a tracking issue.

Requested before merge: none.

The review worktree and branch remain in place to keep the build warm. No PR code was changed.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

I pushed review fixes in `3c4e3b7b8`. Two independent reviews of the first version found six cases. Each one now has a pinning test in `keep_law/incoming_stock_deficits` that fails without its fix, for 16 tests in that module:

1. A program of touch probes only was refused even with the acknowledgment. It is now judged and noted the same way (#108).
2. A torch or wire program keeps the full gate. Unchanged column tops cannot show what such a program left alone (#670).
3. An undercut program keeps the full gate, because an undercut pass lowers no column top (#1444).
4. A probe in a setup other than the judged one never uses that setup's acknowledgment.
5. A program that cuts nothing is now judged on the setup it runs in, not on the first setup's stock. `carry::walk` takes its steps from the program's own operations when nothing is planned. Cutting programs walk exactly as before. This changes the ordinary verdict (acknowledgment off) for programs of probes or torches only.
6. Across setups the walk cannot cross, such a program now refuses by name and writes no NC file. Before, it posted.

Checks on `3c4e3b7b8`:
- Quick gate against `upstream/main`: 353 of 354 steps passed. The one failure was a stale CRLF working copy of the committed `eol=lf` Sinumerik kit file, which this PR does not touch. After the copy was restored, that suite passed 3 of 3.
- Clippy passed on all `camcraft-app` targets with warnings denied.
- 179 of 179 tests passed in 21 related suites.

The PR body is updated, with a changelog line. Ready for a re-check.
merge-ready removed: no review by a collaborator at 3c4e3b7

needs-rework: one requested change before merge - the delta commit (3c4e3b7b) changes the process file .claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md (line 119), and the PR body has no `Process change: yes` line (AGENTS.md - Process changes bump PROCESS_VERSION). One line in the body; no code change.

Ready for the maintainer to merge. Safety-tier re-review. No blocking findings.

This review is of head `3c4e3b7b8`. The earlier review was of `11f18eda3`. The new commit `3c4e3b7b8` changes posting refusal, the stock simulation walk and the incoming-stock report. Thus this review is at the safety tier.

## Earlier findings

The earlier review (`11f18eda3`) had no requested changes. Thus no earlier finding is open.

## NeoTech's request (2026-11-26T03:58Z): done

NeoTech set `needs-rework` because the PR body had no `Process change: yes` line. The commit `3c4e3b7b8` changes the process file `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md:118` (the `set_raw_stock_only` row; line 119 after the merge with main).

- The PR body now has the line `Process change: yes` (body line 37). The head did not change.
- The PR does not edit `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`. This is correct: the merging session bumps it.
- The earlier review did not see the missing line. That was an error of the earlier review.

Thus this request is met, and `needs-rework` is removed with this review.

## What looks good

- `carry::walk` keeps the old step list for each cutting program. `step_setups` reads the program operations only when the plan is empty. Thus a cutting program walks as before. The mutation below shows that the new path is necessary.
- `cuts_nothing_across_setups` adds a refusal only. It never makes a refused program post.
- `report` keeps the full gate for an undercut pass, a torch and a wire. A missing operation or tool gives `None`, which also keeps the full gate.
- A probe in a setup other than the judged setup keeps the full gate.
- The note for the acknowledgment is a `not_judged` note, so the post says it. It is not silent.
- No `unwrap()`, `expect()` or `panic!()` in the new non-test code.
- No golden file and no recorded program changed.

## Results, merged with main (locally)

The checks ran locally in `.claude/worktrees/review-4066`. The trial merge is `6469f6e43`, with upstream main `79ca6a088`. Its first parent is the PR head `3c4e3b7b8`. The merge had no conflict.

- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 355 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled. This includes `ui suites: operations` and `ui suites: shell`.
- Pinning tests: the 16 tests in `keep_law::incoming_stock_deficits` passed (`cargo xtask gate test incoming_stock_deficits --crate app --binary keep_law`).
- Light lane (`cargo xtask gate light`): 6 steps, 0 failed.
- App clippy, all targets, `-D warnings`: passed, with no warnings (run with `--target-dir target/clippy-review`, see the host note).

Extra suites run (by name, in the quick gate):

- `app suites: example_catalog`: passed.
- `app suites: example_catalog_edge_work`: passed.
- `app suites: solid_law_goldens`: passed.
- `app suites: keep_law`: passed.

The diff does not change `testdata/` or the import code. Thus no kernel STEP suite is necessary. The heavy lanes did not run: the current law does not require them at review.

## Mutations (source, local only, restored after each run)

1. Remove the undercut guard in `crates/app/src/stock_sim_incoming.rs:21`. Also remove the `Torch | Wire => return None` arm in `unplanned_probe_setups`. Also remove the `cuts_nothing_across_setups` refusal in `crates/app/src/posting_sim.rs:135`.
   - RED as expected, exactly these 4 tests: `acknowledged_an_undercut_program_keeps_the_full_gate`, `acknowledged_a_torch_program_keeps_the_full_gate`, `a_probe_program_across_setups_the_sim_cannot_cross_refuses`, `a_torch_program_across_setups_the_sim_cannot_cross_refuses`.
   - The other 12 tests stayed GREEN.
2. Disable the empty-plan branch of `step_setups` in `crates/app/src/stock_sim_carry.rs:331`, so that a program that cuts nothing walks from the first setup again.
   - RED as expected, 6 tests: `a_probe_program_uses_its_own_setups_acknowledgement`, `a_probe_program_on_clean_stock_posts_beside_an_idle_deficient_setup`, `an_idle_setup_with_no_stock_leaves_the_probe_judged_on_its_own`, `an_idle_clean_setup_never_hides_the_probes_own_deficits` and the two cross-setup refusal tests.

After the restore, all 16 tests passed again.

## Optional, non-blocking

- `crates/app/src/stock_sim_carry.rs` grows from 383 to 418 lines. This is more than the 400-line rule. A later split along the walk seam can fix it.
- `crates/app/src/stock_sim.rs` was more than 400 lines before this PR. This PR adds lines to it.

## Host note

On this host, a direct `cargo test` or `cargo clippy` in the warm review worktree first failed with `E0463 can't find crate` for external crates (`solidcore`, `boa_engine`). The cause is a stale build cache. The PR does not change these crates. The gate steps did not have this problem. Clippy ran again in a clean target directory.

This PR is a `feat`. By the Pull Request Law, it merges at the next minor cut.

Requested before merge: none.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

left for the maintainer: check 6 skip - feat/post PR; waiting for a cut. The counted re-review at head 3c4e3b7b8 is clean (quick gate 355 steps, 0 failed); the merge remains the maintainer's decision.

Correction: at 04:13Z our review run removed NeoTech's `needs-rework` on head `3c4e3b7b8` and set `merge-ready` on the same head. That was wrong: a collaborator's request for changes on a head stays until a new head or a withdrawal by the reviewer who asked. The labels are restored (`needs-rework` back, `merge-ready` removed). For the record: the `Process change: yes` line NeoTech asked for is now in the PR body; whether that settles the request is NeoTech's call.
